purpose: Foreground disco ball and original gold spotlight with an additional translucent cyan beam from the upper-right side toward lower-left.
compositing: Normal alpha-over; contains actual partial transparency.
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied transparent FRONT PARALLAX LAYER for Eugene's disco card. It currently contains a mirrored disco ball in the UPPER-RIGHT with its golden star glint, and a warm gold spotlight beam shining diagonally inward from the TOP-LEFT. The user requests ONE ADDITIONAL SPOTLIGHT BEAM from ANOTHER DIRECTION and in a DIFFERENT COLOR.

KEEP the existing disco ball, small hanging attachment, colored mirror facets, original golden ball glint and the existing TOP-LEFT GOLDEN SPOTLIGHT exactly in place with the same sizes, colors, angles and transparency. Preserve the entire 1024 x 1536 portrait canvas and registration; do not move, resize, crop, redraw or duplicate the ball or gold beam.

ADD ONE COOL CYAN / TURQUOISE SPOTLIGHT beam entering from off-canvas at the UPPER-RIGHT SIDE EDGE, just BELOW the disco ball, around y=350. Its narrow offscreen origin lies at the right edge rather than emerging from the disco ball. It points DIAGONALLY DOWN AND LEFT toward approximately x=150, y=900, widening gently and fading out as it crosses the upper-middle of the composition. This opposing diagonal must read clearly as light from a different direction than the existing upper-left gold cone. Choose luminous ice-cyan with a subtle blue-turquoise transition so it contrasts visibly with gold while matching the disco palette. The two beams can cross with a restrained soft luminous mixture, but the new beam must not cover the disco ball itself or turn the whole layer into colored fog. No visible lamp fixture is needed.

ALPHA / LIGHT QUALITY: This is a translucent volume of colored light, not an opaque cyan triangle, laser line or painted cloudy backdrop. The beam should have a soft bright narrow origin, smooth directional internal streaks, softly feathered sides, a long tapering fade, and low-to-moderate TRUE ALPHA throughout its body. It will be placed IN FRONT of the character: his face and clothing must remain clearly visible through the light. Keep most of the cyan beam around roughly 10–25 percent opacity, modestly stronger only at its narrow offscreen origin, feathering to zero at edges and its distant lower-left end. Use actual fractional alpha with cyan-colored pixels, suitable for ordinary normal alpha-over compositing, no screen-blend trick or black backing. Do not add a solid dark blue haze or opaque rectangular region. Maintain original transparency in empty spaces and the original ball's opaque facets. Bottom quarter of the canvas should remain empty transparent.

Only the disco ball, its existing glint, the original warm gold upper-left beam and the new opposing cyan beam may appear. NO character, crowd, floor, reflections, extra disco ball, new glitter/confetti, star field, smoke clouds, text, frame or watermark. Preserve original angular mirror-ball illustration style. Output ONE updated full-canvas transparent RGBA PNG. The precise edit is to add the opposing cool cyan light while leaving the existing foreground artwork intact.
